s1.syndrome_frame: cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with metastatic cancer
salient_findings: single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation identified
key_facts: patient is a man in his 40s
patient has stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma
patient has pulmonary and liver metastases
patient has undergone radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
lesion developed in early January 2015
lesion is 4 cm in diameter
lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
histopathological analysis shows normal epidermis
genetic analysis was performed using paired whole-exome sequencing

shortlist.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: cutaneous vascular lesion in a patient with metastatic cancer

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: aggressive vascular tumor that can arise in the setting of chronic lymphedema or radiation therapy

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: vascular tumor associated with immunosuppression and telangiectasias

shortlist.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: benign vascular tumor that can present with telangiectasias

shortlist.label: Bacillary angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: infectious cause of vascular lesions that can resemble telangiectasias

raw.rationale: The presence of a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, along with the histopathological findings of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels and normal epidermis, is consistent with Bacillary angiomatosis. Additionally, the genetic analysis finding of a KDR (VEGFR2) mutation supports this diagnosis, as Bacillary angiomatosis is known to be associated with vascular proliferation and can be linked to genetic alterations in angiogenic pathways.

rejected.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with lymphedema and more aggressive clinical course, which is not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with more rapid growth and destructive lesions, and histopathological analysis would show more atypical cells and disorganized vascular structures

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple lesions and has a distinct histopathological appearance with spindle cell proliferation and slit-like vascular spaces, which is not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
rejected.why: Characterized by a distinct glomeruloid or hobnail appearance on histopathology, which is not mentioned in the vignette
